description:
## Scope: three deliberate-deep refinements. All three are independent of each other; land as separate commits in this order.

### 1. ISS-012 chunking half (the failure-marker half ships in T-028 — check it landed first)
runCrossReview (src/backends/orchestrator.ts:470-485) sends input.content (the full diff) in ONE turn. A diff big enough to be chunked in the main review will likely blow the adjudication turn.
Fix (decided): slice the subject to only the files referenced by the findings under adjudication. Build a per-file map of the diff (split on /^diff --git /m boundaries — same boundary logic chunkDiff uses, src/utils/chunking.ts:65), keep only sections whose path appears in findings[].file, fall back to the FULL diff when no finding has a file. Budget check with estimateTokens (chunking.ts:1) against config.max_chunk_tokens: if the sliced subject STILL exceeds the budget, do NOT multi-turn — fail that adjudication call cleanly so T-028's cross_review_failures marker reports it (honest degradation, bounded cost). Implement the slicing where the composite prepares the crossReview call (deliberation.ts adjudicateDivergent, :262-282), not inside runCrossReview — the orchestrator stays subject-agnostic.

### 2. ISS-014 model override (deliberation.ts ONLY — verified: CrossReviewInput.model already exists at backend.ts:50 and runCrossReview already consumes it at orchestrator.ts:475 `input.model ?? deps.config.model`; no orchestrator change)
deliberatePlan/deliberateCode receive input.model (the caller's override, which by convention applies to the PRIMARY provider only). Thread it: adjudicateDivergent gains a `primaryModel?: string` param (call sites deliberation.ts:302, :332); runAdjudicate gains `model?: string` and passes it in the crossReview input — pass primaryModel ONLY when judge === primary (the secondary always resolves its own default, same rule as reviews).

### 3. ISS-015 verdict/adjudication contract (documentation, minimal code)
Worst-verdict-wins is computed at deliberation.ts:123 (code) and :154 (plan) BEFORE cross-review, so a verdict resting entirely on findings later disputed stays harsh. Decided: do NOT recompute the verdict (synthesis is the caller's job — that is the design). Instead: (a) code comment at both verdict lines stating verdict is pre-adjudication by design; (b) README + review_plan/review_code tool descriptions state: "under deliberate-deep, verdict reflects both providers' independent reviews; adjudications in deliberation.divergent[] are advisory input for your synthesis, not folded into verdict". If during implementation you believe recomputing is needed anyway — don't; file an issue instead.

## Acceptance
(1) Unit test: cross-review subject for findings on file A excludes file B's section; no-file findings get the full diff; over-budget sliced subject produces a cross_review_failures entry, not a crash. (2) Unit test: primary-judge call receives the override model, secondary-judge call does not. (3) Live probe: deliberate-deep on a chunk-forcing large diff (generate one >max_chunk_tokens) completes with adjudications present. Resolve ISS-012, ISS-014, ISS-015.

## House rules
TDD; ESM .js suffixes; no `any`/`as`; Result<T>; mock only leaf/SDK seams; full gate; no AI names in commits.
title: Deliberate-deep polish: cross-review chunking, adjudication model override, verdict-adjudication contract (ISS-012, ISS-014, ISS-015)
